mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility has stabilized at +6.0 to +6.4% across all four weeks, indicating sustained shelter-in-place behavior. This persistent elevation in home-based activity directly suppresses retail-and-recreation mobility by reducing the opportunity set for out-of-home consumption, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +6.0 to +6.4 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL falls below +4% in any of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility has declined consistently from -14.7% to -13.4% across four weeks, signaling sustained avoidance of public transportation. This behavioral shift reduces commute-based retail exposure and signals persistent fear of crowded spaces, which will constrain RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility improves by more than 5 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points on average.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has remained stable at -8.6% to -10.7%, indicating that essential-goods access is constrained but not collapsing. When essential mobility is suppressed but not eliminated, discretionary retail-and-recreation mobility faces a policy-driven ceiling effect. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as restrictions maintain the essential-versus-discretionary distinction.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains between -15% and -5% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range -8.6% to -10.7% across all four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -5%, indicating policy relaxation across both categories.

mechanism_narrative: Parks mobility has oscillated between -4.9% and -8.7%, showing volatile outdoor-activity demand. When parks mobility is suppressed and volatile, it signals uncertainty about outdoor-space safety and availability. This uncertainty, combined with sustained residential elevation, will interact to keep RETAIL_REC depressed as consumers avoid both outdoor recreation and indoor retail simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -7% while RESIDENTIAL remains above +5.5%
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -3% in any week while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -8%, indicating a shift toward outdoor-activity preference that does not translate to retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility has improved from -3.9% (t-3w) to -0.9% (t-1w), then declined to -1.1% (t-0w), showing a stalled recovery. This plateau in workplace return signals that commuting routines have not re-established. Without workplace-anchored mobility, retail-and-recreation footfall will remain suppressed because the weekday retail cycle depends on commuter traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains above -3% but below +2% for three consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -3.9% to -0.9% then declined to -1.1%
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above +5% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points on average despite workplace stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: Retail-and-recreation mobility declined from -9.7% (t-1w) to -11.9% (t-0w), a reversal of the prior week's improvement. This week-on-week deterioration signals an acceleration of restrictions or a behavioral shock. When RETAIL_REC momentum turns negative, it typically persists for at least one additional week as consumer expectations adjust downward.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls by more than 1.5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -9% in the first week after the decision point, contradicting the momentum-persistence hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Transit mobility and workplace mobility are jointly suppressed (TRANSIT -13.4%, WORKPLACES -1.1%), indicating that commuting infrastructure remains offline. The interaction of these two factors creates a dual barrier: no workplace demand and no transit access. This dual suppression will prevent retail-and-recreation recovery because retail depends on commuter-anchored foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -12% AND WORKPLACES remains above -2% simultaneously
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -10% while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises above +3%, indicating a restoration of commuting infrastructure that would support retail recovery.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy mobility has remained stable at -8.6% to -10.7% across four weeks, indicating that essential-goods demand is inelastic and policy-constrained. In a regime of sustained essential-goods suppression, discretionary retail-and-recreation mobility will remain depressed because consumer budgets and time are redirected toward essential procurement, and retail venues remain closed or capacity-restricted.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains below -8% for all four weeks prior to the decision point
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -5% while RETAIL_REC falls below -15%, indicating a decoupling where essential goods recover but retail remains severely suppressed.
